author: Master Tea Blender, Amarkanth Group
excerpt: CTC stands for Crush, Tear, Curl — a mechanical processing method that turns fresh Assam tea leaves into dense, dark granules that brew fast, bold, and dark kadak chai.

content.text: CTC stands for Crush, Tear, Curl. Instead of leaving the tea leaf whole or gently rolling it, fresh Assam tea leaves pass through a series of cylindrical rollers with sharp, counter-rotating teeth. These rollers crush, tear, and curl the leaves into small, hard, uniform granules.

Because these tiny tea granules have a significantly higher surface area per gram than whole leaves, they release dark liquor, rich tannins, and robust flavor almost instantly when boiled. That rapid extraction is precisely why CTC tea (commonly called chai patti or tea powder in India) is the foundational leaf behind everyday milk chai, tea stalls, hotels, and family breakfast rituals across South Asia.
How CTC Tea Is Processed: Step-by-Step

items: 1. Plucking: Fresh green tea leaves (typically two leaves and a bud) are hand-harvested from high-grown Assam estates.
2. Withering: Plucked leaves are spread on long troughs where ambient air reduces moisture content by 30-40%, making the leaves pliable.
3. CTC Processing: Withered leaves are fed into CTC machines where precision rollers crush, tear, and curl them into uniform micro-granules.
4. Oxidation (Fermentation): The damp granules are exposed to controlled humidity and temperature, developing their characteristic deep reddish-brown color and rich, malty aroma.
5. Drying & Firing: Granules pass through hot air dryers to stop oxidation and lock in moisture levels below 3%.
6. Grading & Sorting: Vibrating mesh screens sort the tea into distinct commercial grades based on particle size.

content.text: CTC Tea vs. Orthodox Tea: What Is the Difference?

While Orthodox tea leaves are kept whole or semi-whole to yield delicate, floral, and subtle notes (ideal for drinking light without milk), CTC tea is engineered specifically for strength, deep liquor color, and compatibility with milk and sugar. CTC tea granules stand up boldly against milk without losing their tea character.

items.question: Is CTC tea good for milk tea?
items.answer: Yes! CTC tea is the absolute gold standard for milk tea and kadak chai. Its high tannin density ensures the tea flavor cuts through milk without tasting watery.

items.question: How much CTC tea should I use per cup?
items.answer: Use approximately 1 rounded teaspoon (2.5 to 3 grams) of CTC tea per standard cup of water/milk.

items.question: Is CTC tea the same as tea dust?
items.answer: Not exactly. Dust is simply one specific fine grade of CTC tea. CTC encompasses larger Broken Pekoe (BP) and Fannings (PF) granules as well.

title: How to Make Kadak Chai with CTC Tea at Home (Step by Step)
metaTitle: How to Make Kadak Chai with CTC Tea (Step by Step)
metaDescription: Make strong, tea-stall style kadak chai at home with CTC tea. Simple water-to-milk ratio, boiling technique, and tips to avoid bitter chai.
keywords: how to make kadak chai, CTC tea recipe, tea stall style chai at home, kadak chai patti, milk tea ratio, cardamom ginger tea recipe
author: Culinary Tea Specialist
excerpt: Learn the secret ratio, decoction simmering technique, and spice infusion timings to brew authentic, tea-stall style kadak chai at home.

content.text: Kadak chai is not just tea — it is an emotion. Achieving that signature deep amber color, rich malty aroma, and comforting body requires high-quality Assam CTC tea granules and proper brewing chemistry.
The Perfect Golden Ratio (2 Standard Cups)

items: Water: 1 cup (200 ml) filtered water
Milk: 1 cup (200 ml) fresh full-fat milk
CTC Tea Patti: 2 rounded teaspoons (5–6 grams) Amarkanth Premium CTC Tea
Sugar: 1.5 to 2 teaspoons (to taste)
Aromatics (Optional): ½ inch fresh ginger (crushed) & 2 green cardamom pods (gently cracked)

content.text: Step-by-Step Kadak Chai Brewing Method

items: Step 1 (Water & Spice Decoction): Bring 1 cup of water to a rolling boil in a saucepan. Add crushed ginger and cracked cardamom. Simmer on medium heat for 60 seconds so essential oils infuse into the water.
Step 2 (Tea Extraction): Add 2 tsp of Amarkanth Assam CTC tea. Lower the heat to medium-low and boil the tea decoction for 90 seconds until the water turns dark reddish-brown.
Step 3 (Milk & Sugar): Pour in 1 cup of full-fat milk and add sugar. Increase heat to medium-high.

Step 4 (Rolling Simmer): Allow the chai to come to a full rolling boil (letting the foam rise near the rim 2 to 3 times, swirling the pan gently). Reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 minutes to thicken milk and blend flavors.
Step 5 (Strain & Serve): Strain through a fine mesh strainer directly into hot clay kulhads or cups. Serve steaming hot with biscuits or snacks!

content.text: 4 Common Chai Mistakes & How to Fix Them

items: Mistake 1: Adding Milk First. Boiling tea leaves directly in milk coats the granules with fat, preventing full extraction. Always boil CTC tea in water first!
Mistake 2: Over-Boiling After Milk. Boiling chai for more than 4 minutes after milk is added causes milk proteins to burn and tannins to turn harsh and bitter.
Mistake 3: Using Stale Chai Patti. CTC tea exposed to air loses volatile aromatics within weeks. Keep tea stored in airtight containers away from light.
Mistake 4: Low Quantity of Leaf. Trying to get strength by over-boiling a small amount of tea makes chai bitter. Add more CTC leaf instead of boiling longer!

title: Buying CTC Tea in Bulk: 8 Things to Check Before You Order

author: B2B Trade Manager, Amarkanth Group
excerpt: Essential B2B checklist for tea stall owners, hotel managers, distributors, and bulk buyers evaluating CTC tea suppliers in India.

content.text: If you operate a commercial tea stall network, hotel, restaurant, café chain, or FMCG distribution business, CTC tea is one of your most critical recurring inventory items. Purchasing bulk CTC tea requires checking beyond just price per kilogram.
The 8-Point Bulk CTC Buyer's Checklist

items: 1. Grade Consistency Across Batches: Ensure your supplier guarantees consistent mesh particle sizing (BP, PF, PD, Dust) so every cup you serve has identical color and cup strength.
2. Pre-Order Sample Testing: Always test pre-order samples under actual operational conditions — using your commercial milk quality, local water hardness, and boiling equipment.
3. Moisture-Proof Packaging: Verify that bulk sacks or master cartons use multi-wall paper with food-grade aluminum foil or inner poly liners to protect against moisture absorption.
4. Stock Freshness & Packing Date: Ask for garden invoice dates and packaging batch numbers. Fresh CTC tea retains essential oils for 12 months when stored sealed.
5. FSSAI License & Lab Compliance: Confirm that the manufacturer holds an active FSSAI License (e.g. FSSAI Lic No: 11423870000024) and complies with pesticide and heavy metal safety limits.
6. Evaluate Cost Per Cup (Not Just Cost Per Kg): A higher-density Assam CTC tea that yields 400 cups per kg is far more profitable than a cheap, weak tea yielding only 250 cups per kg.
7. Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) & Lead Times: Agree on manageable MOQs (e.g. 50 kg to 500 kg) and fast dispatch SLA timelines to prevent out-of-stock emergencies.
8. Transparent GST Invoicing & Payment Terms: Demand GST tax invoices with explicit credit/COD terms and transparent freight cost breakdowns.

title: How to Store CTC Tea So It Stays Fresh for 365 Days

keywords: how to store CTC tea, tea storage tips, keep chai patti fresh, airtight tea container
author: Quality Assurance Team
excerpt: 4 simple rules to protect your chai patti from humidity, air exposure, light, and kitchen odors to maintain garden-fresh flavor.

content.text: CTC tea granules are hygroscopic — meaning they readily absorb moisture, ambient humidity, and surrounding odors from your kitchen. Proper storage is essential to prevent your chai patti from tasting flat or stale.
The 4 Enemies of Tea Freshness

items: 1. Air (Oxygen): Exposure to air causes essential tea oils to oxidize, turning brisk tea flat.
2. Moisture: Humidity causes CTC granules to absorb dampness, leading to mold or loss of liquor strength.
3. Light & Heat: Sunlight and stove heat degrade tea polyphenols and cardamom aromatics.
4. Strong Odors: Storing tea near spices, onions, or cleaning supplies causes tea to absorb unwanted smells.

content.text: Best Practices for Storing CTC Tea

items: Use opaque glass jars, stainless steel canisters, or heavy-duty airtight tin containers.
Keep the tea container in a cool, dark kitchen pantry away from stoves and direct sunlight.
Always close the zip-slider or inner seal immediately after scooping tea.
